# authwise_scim_tokens (Data Source)

A bearer token a directory pushes users and groups with, for one `authwise_scim_connection`. kit creates it and returns it once, as `<id>_<secret>`, so **the token is kept in state**, marked sensitive: protect the state as you would the token, since anyone who reads it can write the realm's users. Paste `secret` into the directory with the connection's `base_url`. There is no update: changing `scim_connection_id` or `expires_at` replaces the token, and the old one stops working when it is destroyed. To rotate, add a second token, move the directory to it, then remove the first. This data source lists every one under a parent.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `realm_id` (String) Parent identifier `realm_id`; overrides the provider default.
- `tenant_id` (String) Parent identifier `tenant_id`; overrides the provider default.

### Read-Only

- `scim_tokens` (Attributes List) Every scim_token under the parent, in the order the API lists them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--scim_tokens))

<a id="nestedatt--scim_tokens"></a>
### Nested Schema for `scim_tokens`

Read-Only:

- `created_at` (String)
- `expires_at` (String)
- `last_used_at` (String)
- `name` (String) Full resource name.
- `scim_connection_id` (String)
- `scim_token_id` (String) Server-assigned resource id — the last segment of `name`, and what other resources' `*_id` attributes take.
